outils.name: pw_session
outils.title: Pw Session
outils.description:
Manage the Playwright browser session lifecycle (Chromium by default; the
service's BROWSER_ENGINE can select firefox or webkit - action="health"
reports the engine in use).

action= :
  start       : open a session. Required: url=.
                SECURE SESSION (REQUIRED to log in with a saved login): when the
                user supplies ⟦creds:TOKEN@ORIGIN⟧ (the /creds command), open
                the session with pw_session(action="start", url=…, secure=true)
                (add creds="TOKEN" when the site uses HTTP auth), then call
                pw_login(session_id, creds="TOKEN", username_target=…,
                password_target=…, submit_target=…): it types the login for you
                and empties the page (you never type or read a password).
                A secure session is a NEW dedicated headless browser (own process and
                clipboard, never a reused session), with strict TLS (an
                untrusted certificate fails to load), and it stays locked for
                its whole life. Targets must be semantic (role+name, label,
                placeholder, text, test_id, alt, title, or a ref from pw_find):
                css= and xpath= are refused. NOT available in a secure session:
                pw_page eval / pdf / wait / element / extract_table with a CSS
                selector, pw_mock, pw_recorder, interception, poll_until,
                dispatch_event, trigger_framework_update, watch_changes,
                save_state / load_state, trace / HAR / video, drag, clipboard
                shortcuts (Ctrl/Cmd + a c x v z y, Shift+Insert, Copy/Paste/Undo…), the middle and right mouse buttons, pw_a11y with a
                selector scope. Password fields are masked in screenshots and
                their value is never returned. If the quota of open sessions is
                reached the start fails (session_quota_reached): stop one
                first, nothing is closed for you. Open a secure session for
                logging in and nothing else.
                HTTP AUTH (Basic AND Digest) → creds="TOKEN" (the part before
                the @ of the ⟦creds:TOKEN@ORIGIN⟧) HERE, at start: it makes the
                session secure. The token is bound to ONE exact origin
                (scheme://host:port): url= must be on that origin. Credentials
                are set at context creation (httpCredentials) and can NOT be
                added afterwards via a goto. A certificate that is not trusted
                is refused, unless the user ticked "accept an unverified
                certificate" on that /creds entry (every response then says
                tls_verification="disabled", and every request to another
                origin is blocked). NEVER ask for a password in clear
                and never pass one. If a page returns 401, ask the user for
                /creds, then start WITH creds=. No popup is shown.
                Without secure=: use load_state_id= to resume cookies from a
                saved session.
                IDEMPOTENT PER USER (normal sessions only): one browser
                instance per user. If you already have a normal session, start
                REUSES it and opens url= in a NEW TAB (returns reused=true +
                tab_index). Use pw_page with
                action="tabs"/"tab_switch" to list/switch between your tabs.
                EMULATION (optional): device="iPhone 13"|"Pixel 7"|"iPad Mini"…
                OR viewport="1280x800"; plus locale=, timezone=,
                color_scheme="dark", touch=true. Default: desktop 1920x1080.
                TESTING (optional, never with secure=): isolated=true (FRESH
                context, no reuse — for reproducible tests) ; trace=true
                (then action="trace_export" → trace_url viewable via
                `npx playwright show-trace`) ; record_video=true (video_urls
                returned by action="stop").
  trace_export: stop le tracing et renvoie trace_url (si trace=true au start).
  stop        : close session. Required: session_id=.
  save_state  : save cookies/localStorage. Reusable via load_state_id.
  list        : list active sessions. Optional url_filter= (substring match
                on URL or domain) — returns matching sessions only.
  cleanup     : close all sessions + kill zombie browser processes.
  health      : browser service status: engine, uptime, your sessions
                (sessions=[...]) and session_count (all accounts).

PROTOCOL: you get a single instance. Call start whenever you need a URL —
it reuses your existing instance and opens a new tab rather than failing.
Switch between tabs with pw_page(action="tab_switch", index=N).

SYNONYMS (all pw_* tools): action= == op= == do=, value= == v=, target= == selector=.

creds.description: TOKEN of a ⟦creds:TOKEN@ORIGIN⟧ the user supplied (the part before the @): HTTP auth credentials, for its exact origin only. Makes the session secure.

secure.description: Open a SECURE session: a NEW dedicated browser, strict TLS, locked tools and semantic targets only. Required before pw_login. Implied by creds=.

anyOf.description: Result of pw_session — start/list/close/info on Playwright sessions.

Typed shape of the error envelope produced by ``_toolkit.err()``.

Mirrors the error contract the chat frontend parses :
  * ``ok`` is the discriminator (False = failure),
  * ``error`` is a stable machine code (snake_case),
  * ``message`` is the human-readable text,
  * ``fix`` is an optional hint how to recover.

Tools declare their return type as ``Union[<SuccessModel>,
ErrEnvelope]`` so FastMCP generates a discriminated union schema
the LLM can pattern-match on the ``ok`` field. The runtime
wire format is unchanged — both branches serialise to the same
JSON dict the frontend already reads.

``extra='allow'`` because ``err()`` lets each call site attach
context (``cmd``, ``path``, ``expected``, ``actual``, …) — these
are kept for the LLM but aren't part of the strict schema.

retryable.description: True iff a retry might succeed (transient error).

outils.name: pw_find
outils.title: Pw Find
outils.description:
Locate element(s). Returns {count, matches:[{tag,text,visible,ref}]}.

include_frames=true : ALSO searches inside iframes (native Playwright
  page.frames()). Each match then carries `frame:{name,url}` and its `ref`
  stays actionable by pw_act (re-resolved on the right frame). Essential for
  legacy UIs built on iframes (framed login forms, etc.).

PREFERRED FORMAT — single target string (DSL):
  pw_find(target="role=button|name=Login")
  pw_find(target="label=Email")
  pw_find(target="placeholder=Search")
  pw_find(target="text=Welcome")
  pw_find(target="test_id=cta")
  pw_find(target="role=row|nth=0")
  pw_find(target="css=div.product-card", max=20)

LEGACY (still supported): pw_find(role="button", name="Login").

Strategy preference (most → least robust):
  role+name > label > placeholder > test_id > text > css > xpath

The returned `ref` can be passed to pw_act(target="ref=loc_xxx"). It stays
valid `ref_ttl_s` seconds (300) and is reusable — but on content that shifts
or disappears, re-run pw_find right before acting.
If you call pw_find with no target/selector, it returns smart_inspect (lite).

selector=  : raw CSS, synonym of target= (wrapped as "css=…"). target wins.

max=       : cap on locator matches returned (default 5).
max_items= : pagination cap, same knob as pw_page/pw_act. >0 caps the
             no-target smart_inspect fallback AND overrides `max` for
             matches (one consistent name across the pw_* API).

In a SECURE session (pw_session secure=true) css=, xpath= and selector= are refused: target by role+name, label, placeholder, text, test_id, alt or title.

anyOf.description: Result of pw_find — locate one or many DOM elements via the DSL or selector.

count.description: How many matches were returned (capped by max=).

total.description: How many elements matched before the cap.

matches.description: Each {tag, text, role, visible, enabled, ref, xpath, in_viewport, frame?}.

ref_ttl_s.description: Seconds a returned `ref` stays valid on the service — re-run pw_find after that, or sooner on content that shifts/disappears.

ref_reusable.description: True: the same ref can be passed to several pw_act calls until it expires.

outils.name: pw_act
outils.title: Pw Act
outils.description:
Act on an element or page.

PREFERRED — target DSL (single string):
  pw_act(sid, action="click", target="role=button|name=Login")
  pw_act(sid, action="click", target="text=Add to cart")
  pw_act(sid, action="fill",  target="label=Email",       value="me@x.com")
  pw_act(sid, action="press", value="Enter")       # no target = current focus
  pw_act(sid, action="select", target="label=Country", option_label="France")
  pw_act(sid, action="pick",  target="css=#city", option_label="Lyon")  # ANY dropdown
  pw_act(sid, action="scroll", direction="down", amount=800)   # page
  pw_act(sid, action="goto",  url="https://example.com")
  pw_act(sid, action="click", target="ref=loc_abc")  # ref from pw_find
  pw_act(sid, action="drag",   target="css=#column-a", to="css=#column-b")   # drag & drop
  pw_act(sid, action="expand", target="role=treeitem|name=Tables")           # open a tree node

SYNONYMS (all pw_* tools): action= == do=, value= == v=, selector= == target=.

TARGET MATCHING: the target is counted before acting.
  - no match after ~2 s -> element_not_found right away, with `suggestions`
    (targets with a close name, else of the same role). Wait first with
    pw_wait when the element shows up late.
  - several matches -> acts on the FIRST, returns matched=N + warning.
    strict=true refuses instead (ambiguous_target + `candidates`, each with
    a ref). Add |nth=K (0-based) to the target to choose one.
  - name= is matched as the WHOLE name first (case-insensitive), then as a
    substring ("Start" may hit "Restart": name_match="substring" + warning).
  Each gesture waits up to 8 s for its element to be actionable (same
  default as pw_chain), so the service error arrives before the tool timeout.

AUTH NOTE: for a page behind HTTP auth (Basic/Digest), goto takes NO
credentials. Open the session with: pw_session(action="start",
url=…, creds="TOKEN"). A goto on such a page returns the
auth_hint field as a reminder.

SECRETS: a saved login ⟦creds:TOKEN@ORIGIN⟧ is never typed by a gesture. secret=
was removed: use pw_login (one call that fills, submits and empties the page)
on a session opened with pw_session(action="start", url=…, secure=true).
Never ask for a password in clear and never put one in value=.

Actions (action=):
  click | fill | press | hover | check | uncheck | focus | type | clear
  dblclick | rclick | goto | back | forward | reload
  upload     : put files in an <input type=file> (target=). files= : paths
               inside your sandbox /work (["report.pdf"], ["/work/a.csv"]) or
               {"name", "content_base64", "mime_type"?} objects. Nothing
               outside /work is readable (file_not_found, files_required).
  select     : NATIVE <select> only. Prefer option_label= (what you SEE) or
               option_value=. The options are listed in pw_page("inspect").
  pick       : ANY dropdown — native <select>, autocomplete input, or a custom
               div/ul/role=listbox one. Opens it and clicks the option for you.
               Use this when the control is not a real <select>.
  scroll     : NO target  → scrolls the PAGE (direction=, amount=). When the
               page itself cannot scroll (max_y=0 — GWT/desktop-like layouts
               scroll INSIDE a panel), the largest scrollable container is
               scrolled instead and named in `container` (strategy=
               container-scroll); target it explicitly next time. The list
               of scrollable panels is in pw_page("inspect").scrollables.
               target= + direction= → scrolls INSIDE that container.
               target= alone → brings the element into view.
  drag       : drag target= and drop it on to= (DSL). Pointer drag first
               (Playwright dragTo), then synthetic HTML5 drag events when
               the drop did not land. Without to=, direction=/amount= drag
               by an offset in pixels.
  expand | collapse : open / close a tree node or disclosure (GWT CellTree,
               ARIA tree, accordion). A plain click on a tree item usually
               only SELECTS it: this tries the toggle icon, then
               focus + ArrowRight/ArrowLeft, then dblclick, and VERIFIES
               aria-expanded. Result: expanded_before / expanded / method.
               (A click on a tree item also reports `expanded` so you can
               see it did not open.)

wait_after= : "network" (wait networkidle, max 6s) | "selector:#x" |
              "text:Welcome" | <int ms>. Use after navigation-triggering clicks.

value= : text for fill/type, key for press (Enter/Tab/Escape/etc).
option_label= / option_value= : for select/pick. option_label is the visible
     text; option_value is the underlying value=. Passing the visible text as
     value= still works but is guessed. Both return `selected` (the option
     really chosen); option_not_found lists the available `options`.
direction= : down|up|left|right (scroll). amount= : pixels, default 500.

observe= : when true (default) the result carries `page_after` — a fresh
     lite snapshot of the page AFTER the action, so you SEE the outcome in
     THIS call (no separate pw_page(action="inspect") needed). Set false only for
     speed-critical sequences where you do not need to see the result.

max_items= : cap on the interactive elements listed in `page_after`
     (default 25, clamped 1-200). Lower it (e.g. 5-10) to save tokens on
     dense pages when you only need confirmation the action landed.

files.description: upload: paths inside /work, or {name, content_base64, mime_type?} objects.

strict.description: Refuse a target that matches several elements (ambiguous_target with the candidates) instead of acting on the first.

anyOf.description: Result of pw_act — click / fill / type / press / select / hover / drag / expand…

target.description: DSL or selector that was acted upon.

strategy.description: How the element was reached: ref | by_official | smart:<strategy> | page-scroll | container-scroll | keyboard.

resolved_selector.description: The Playwright expression the service actually used (e.g. getByRole('button', { name: /Login/i }).first()).

attempts.description: Ordered resolution attempts {via, ok, error?, ms?} — shows when the official locator failed and a fallback landed.

selected.description: select/pick: the option really chosen {value, label, index}.

expanded.description: click/expand/collapse on a tree item or disclosure: aria-expanded AFTER the action (null when the element declares none).

page_after.description: Lite snapshot of the page after the action (observe=true).

outils.name: pw_page
outils.title: Pw Page
outils.description:
Page-level operations (no element target by default).

OPERATIONS (action=):
  inspect    : compact semantic map of the page.
               level= lite|nav|full (default lite — saves ~70% tokens).
                 lite : idx, type, role, name, text, selector, in_viewport
                 nav  : + form structures + href + region
                 full : all fields incl. colors, rect
               Each interactive carries `role` + accessible `name`. PREFER
               building targets from them — target="role=<role>|name=<name>"
               is the most robust locator (resolves via getByRole). Fall
               back to `selector` only when role/name are empty.
               A `<select>` always carries its `options` — pass one of those
               labels to pw_act(action="select", option_label=…).
               `detected_by` means the element was found by heuristic (cursor,
               widget class) and has NO declared role: target it BY TEXT.
               `expanded` tells you whether a dropdown is already open.
               include_frames=True : ALSO lists what is inside <iframe>s
                 (each item carries `frame`). Reach those via
                 pw_find(include_frames=true) → ref → pw_act(target="ref=…").
               since_step=N : returns ONLY elements changed since step N
                              (use payload.screenshot_step from a previous
                              call; cuts ~80% of tokens on stable pages).
               viewport_only=True : drops offscreen elements. The result
                 says what it DROPPED: `candidates_total` and
                 `omitted:{offscreen,hidden,too_small,over_max}` — when the
                 element you expect is missing, look there before
                 concluding it does not exist (raise max_items, or
                 viewport_only=False).
               max_items=30 : caps returned interactives count.
               skip_screenshot=True (default in lite) : no PNG written.
               pierce_shadow=True : reaches inside open shadow roots.
                 Interactive shadow elements are listed inline (each carries
                 in_shadow + shadow_host); a shadow root that holds only TEXT
                 (a web component with no controls) is listed as a
                 `shadow-content` item (in_shadow=true, its text as name), and
                 `shadow:[{host,text,interactive}]` summarizes every host.
                 `shadow_hosts` counts the components seen.
               `scrollables` is ALWAYS present ({selector, h, sh, top,
                 in_viewport}). Empty [] = the page itself scrolls (or nothing
                 does); non-empty = an inner panel scrolls — scroll INSIDE one
                 with pw_act(action="scroll", target="css=<selector>",
                 direction="down"). A page scroll that hits max_y:0 auto-scrolls
                 the largest panel and names it in `container`.
  screenshot : viewport capture, OR element-cropped if target= provided.
               full_page=True for full document (heavy, use sparingly).
               Returns {screenshot, screenshot_url, screenshot_step}.
  wait       : wait for an element to be visible. Required: target= (or selector=).
  eval       : run JS (value=script). Result capped at ~50 KB; over → preview.
  extract    : extract HTML TABLES (tables only — use "text" for prose).
               target= narrows to ONE table; without it, the first one.
  element    : everything about ONE element — all attributes, computed
               cursor/pointer-events/z-index, readOnly, contentEditable, and
               every <option> of a select. THE call to make when a click or a
               fill did not do what you expected. Required: target=.
  frames     : list the <iframe>s of the page (url, name, index).
  text       : extract textContent. Optional target=/selector= (default: whole page).
               include_frames=True : appends the text of each <iframe> (their
               content NEVER appears in the parent document's text).
  tabs       : list tabs (`active` = index of the tab actions run on).
  tab_new    : open tab (value=url). It opens in the BACKGROUND: actions keep
               running on the current tab unless switch=true. The result gives
               the new tab_index and `active`.
  tab_switch : index= required.
  tab_close  : index= required.
               A link or script that opens a new window (target=_blank,
               window.open) adds a tab WITHOUT switching to it: the result of
               that action carries opened_tab {index, url, switch_with} - call
               pw_page(action="tab_switch", index=...) to act on it.
  network    : recent network requests log — document + XHR/fetch, each
               {dir:REQ|RES, method, url, type, host, same_origin, status,
               postData}. Same-origin and document entries are kept first
               when the log exceeds max= (default 50); `by_host` counts
               everything, `total` is the size before the cap.
               value= filters on a URL substring.
  pdf        : export PDF.

SYNONYMS (all pw_* tools): action= == op=, value= == v=, target= == selector=.

EXAMPLES:
  pw_page(sid, action="inspect")                          # lite, viewport only
  pw_page(sid, action="inspect", level="full")            # exhaustive (heavy)
  pw_page(sid, action="inspect", since_step=3)            # diff since step 3
  pw_page(sid, action="screenshot", target="role=dialog") # cropped to dialog
  pw_page(sid, action="eval", value="return document.title")

In a SECURE session (pw_session secure=true): eval, pdf and raw selector= are refused; password fields are masked in screenshots and their value is never returned.

anyOf.description:
Result of pw_page — inspect / screenshot / wait / eval / extract / text / tabs / network / pdf.

CONTRAT — ``status`` accepte un ENTIER (code HTTP d'une navigation) OU une
CHAÎNE : le service Node répond ``{"status": "success"}`` (screenshot,
onglets, pdf) et ``{"status": "found"}`` (wait). Typé ``int`` seul, le
schéma de sortie rejetterait ces réponses côté client MCP (``-32602 …
status must be integer``) alors que l'action a réussi.

status.description: HTTP status of the last navigation (int), or the service outcome ('success', 'found').

screenshot.description: screenshot: PNG file name on the browser service.

screenshot_url.description: screenshot: app-relative URL serving that PNG (/api/playwright/screenshot/<file>).

screenshot_step.description: Step counter of the session (each call also writes step_<sid>_<N>.png).

outils.name: pw_dialog
outils.title: Pw Dialog
outils.description:
Decide in advance how the next native dialog will be answered.

Native dialogs (alert / confirm / prompt) freeze the page until they are
answered, so the browser answers them for you: it ACCEPTS everything by
default. That default means you can never cancel a confirm, and never answer
a prompt (it gets an empty string). Arm a different answer BEFORE the click
that opens the dialog.

action= :
  accept : accept the next dialog. text= is the answer for a prompt.
  dismiss: cancel it (the "Cancel" button of a confirm).
  status : what is currently armed, and the last dialog seen
           ({type, message, action}) — use it to READ what the page asked.
  reset  : back to the default (accept).

times= : how many dialogs this policy covers (default 1, max 20). Useful for
         a flow that chains several confirms.
sticky=true : keep the policy until action="reset" (times= is then ignored).

status returns {armed, last, seen, history (last 10 dialogs), last_policy
(armed|default), default_when_unarmed:"accept", sticky}.

This call returns IMMEDIATELY — it arms a policy, it does not wait.

EXAMPLE — cancel a deletion:
  pw_dialog(sid, action="dismiss")
  pw_act(sid, action="click", target="role=button|name=Delete")
  pw_dialog(sid, action="status")   # → last: {type:"confirm", message:"Sure?"}

outils.name: pw_wait
outils.title: Pw Wait
outils.description:
Wait — for an element to DISAPPEAR, for a dynamic condition, or a fixed pause.

TWO MODES:
  1. Fixed pause — pw_wait(seconds=3)
     Sleeps N seconds (max 300). No session/target needed. Use sparingly (for
     an animation or a rate-limit); prefer a condition wait when you can.
  2. Condition wait — pw_wait(session_id=..., target=..., condition=...)
     Polls until the condition holds or max_wait_s elapses. Requires session_id
     and target= (DSL) or selector= (CSS/text/xpath).

CONDITIONS (default 'hidden'):
  hidden            : element gone / invisible  ← wait for a spinner/overlay/modal to vanish
  visible           : element appears and is visible
  attached          : element exists in the DOM (visible or not)
  detached          : element removed from the DOM
  text_contains     : element text contains expected_text=
  text_changes      : element text differs from its value when the wait began
  count_increases   : more elements match target= than at start
  count_decreases   : fewer elements match target= than at start
  attribute_changes : attribute= changes (or equals expected_value= when given)

RETURNS {ok, mode, condition, status, elapsed_ms, via, polled_value}. If the
condition is not met within max_wait_s, returns ok=False with timed_out=True —
a NORMAL outcome (the element simply never disappeared), not an error; decide
your next step from it. `polled_value` ({count, text, attr, visible}) is what
the element showed LAST — read it before retrying with another condition.

EXAMPLES:
  pw_wait(seconds=2)                                                       # fixed pause
  pw_wait(session_id=s, target="css=.spinner", condition="hidden")         # wait to disappear
  pw_wait(session_id=s, target="role=dialog", condition="hidden", max_wait_s=20)
  pw_wait(session_id=s, selector="#status", condition="text_contains", expected_text="Done")

The target is resolved EXACTLY like pw_expect (same by_*/ref locator on the
service, same fallback ladder on a raw selector), so a wait and the expect
that follows always look at the same element. Waits poll in short chunks, so
they never block other browser calls on the same session and never trip a
request timeout.

anyOf.description:
Result of pw_wait — wait for a dynamic condition or a fixed duration.

outils.name: pw_expect
outils.title: Pw Expect
outils.description:
Assert a condition. Returns {pass: bool, actual, expected, screenshot_on_fail?}.

ELEMENT ASSERTIONS (require target=):
  visible      : element exists and is visible.
  hidden       : element does not exist OR is invisible.
  enabled      : element is interactable.
  disabled     : element is disabled.
  checked      : checkbox/radio is checked.
  unchecked    : checkbox/radio is not checked.
  text-equals  : element textContent == value (trimmed, normalized).
  text-contains: element textContent contains value.
  value-equals : input value == value.
  count-eq     : exactly value (int) elements match the target.
  count-gte    : at least value (int) elements match.
  attr-equals  : attribute (value="attr=foo") equals (value="attr=foo|val=bar").
                 Use compound DSL: target="role=link|name=Docs",
                 value="attr=href|val=/docs".

PAGE ASSERTIONS (no target):
  url-equals    : page.url() == value.
  url-contains  : page.url() contains value.
  url-matches   : page.url() matches regex value.
  title-contains: document.title contains value.

  pw_expect(sid, action="visible", target="role=alert|name=Saved")
  pw_expect(sid, action="text-equals", target="css=h1.title", value="Welcome John")
  pw_expect(sid, action="count-eq", target="role=row", value="5")
  pw_expect(sid, action="url-contains", value="/dashboard")
  pw_expect(sid, action="disabled", target="role=button|name=Submit")

SYNONYMS (all pw_* tools): action= == assertion=, value= == v=, target= == selector=.

This is the primitive for IHM testing. Combine multiple expects to build
an assertion suite. Failures include a screenshot and a hint.

outils.name: pw_chain
outils.title: Pw Chain
outils.description:
Execute multiple actions in a single round-trip (max 30).

actions= : list of {action, target?, value?, key?, url?, wait_after?, ms?}
  action values: click | fill | type | press | select | check | wait | scroll | goto | hover
  (per-step synonyms accepted: action|do|type, value|v)

EXAMPLES:
  # A saved login (⟦creds:…⟧) is never typed in a chain: secret= was removed,
  # use pw_login (secure session, see pw_session).

  # Wait + verify pattern:
  pw_chain(session_id, actions=[
    {"action": "wait", "ms": 500},
    {"action": "click", "target": "test_id=continue"},
  ])

page_after}. ok=false when a step failed — read `results` (code, alternatives +
screenshot when enabled). Each step waits up to 8 s for its element (same
default as pw_act); a step whose target matches nothing fails fast with
code=element_not_found and `alternatives` (targets with a close name). observe=true (default) attaches `page_after`, a
lite snapshot taken AFTER the last step (max_items= caps it) — the same
grounding pw_act gives; set observe=false for speed-critical sequences.
Use this when you have a deterministic sequence to save 5-10x tool-call latency.

outils.name: pw_login
outils.title: Pw Login
outils.description:
Log in with a login the user supplied as ⟦creds:TOKEN@ORIGIN⟧ (the /creds command).
You never type a password: this ONE call fills the fields, submits and empties
the page again, without giving you control in between.

Prerequisite: the session must be a SECURE session opened with
pw_session(action="start", url=…, secure=true) (see pw_session). On any other
session the call is refused (secret_requires_secure_session) before the token is
used.

  pw_login(session_id, creds="TOKEN",
           username_target="label=Email",          # optional
           password_target="label=Password",       # optional
           submit_target="role=button|name=Sign in",  # optional
           wait_for="role=heading|name=Dashboard")    # optional

creds=           : TOKEN, the part before the @ of the ⟦creds:TOKEN@ORIGIN⟧
                   (the whole marker is accepted too).
password_target= : the password field. username_target= : the username field.
                   At least one of the two. Semantic targets only (role+name,
                   label, placeholder, text, test_id, alt, title, or a ref
                   from pw_find) - never css= or xpath=. Each must match
                   exactly ONE VISIBLE element (a hidden field or several
                   matches are refused); the password goes only into a real
                   <input type="password">, the username into a text field.
submit_target=   : the button to click; without it Enter is pressed in the
                   last field filled. The form must POST to the origin the
                   token is bound to (a GET form or another origin is refused).
wait_for=        : target that shows up when the login worked. Without it the
                   call ends on a navigation or when the field disappears or is
                   emptied, within about 40 s.

Multi-step sites (identifier first, password on the next page): call
pw_login(username_target=…, submit_target=…) for step 1, then
pw_login(password_target=…, submit_target=…) for step 2. Each call uses one
of the token's usages.

The fields are checked BEFORE the token is used and the secret is typed only if
the frame holding the field is on the exact origin the token is bound to.
Whatever happens (success, failure, timeout), once the form is submitted every
document that received the secret is REPLACED by a fresh one (the page is
loaded again with a plain GET, never a reload; cookies are kept, in-memory page
state is lost). If a document cannot be replaced its tab is closed, and if that
fails the whole secure session is closed (outcome=session_closed): open a new
one. No other call on the session is served meanwhile (login_in_progress).
Returns {ok, outcome: navigated|field_gone|wait_for|no_change|blocked|
session_closed, url, title, documents_replaced, opened_tab?, page_after}; url,
title and every text are purged of the exact secret. ok=false /
outcome=no_change: nothing changed after the submit (wrong login, extra step,
2FA) - read page_after. LIMITS: the site itself holds the secret while it is
typed and submitted; an identifier that the site displays back (a greeting)
stays readable, only the exact value is purged; page state held in memory
only is lost by the replacement.
NEVER ask the user for a password in
clear. If the token is expired or exhausted, ask the user for /creds again.

creds.description: TOKEN of a ⟦creds:TOKEN@ORIGIN⟧ the user supplied (the part before the @).

password_target.description: Password field (semantic target, one visible element).

username_target.description: Username field (semantic target, one visible element).

submit_target.description: Submit button (semantic target); default: Enter in the last field.

wait_for.description: Semantic target that appears once logged in.

anyOf.description: Result of pw_login — click / fill / type / press / select / hover / drag / expand…

target.description: DSL or selector that was acted upon.

strategy.description: How the element was reached: ref | by_official | smart:<strategy> | page-scroll | container-scroll | keyboard.

resolved_selector.description: The Playwright expression the service actually used (e.g. getByRole('button', { name: /Login/i }).first()).

attempts.description: Ordered resolution attempts {via, ok, error?, ms?} — shows when the official locator failed and a fallback landed.

selected.description: select/pick: the option really chosen {value, label, index}.

expanded.description: click/expand/collapse on a tree item or disclosure: aria-expanded AFTER the action (null when the element declares none).

page_after.description: Lite snapshot of the page after the action (observe=true).

outils.description:
Record session actions and dump them as a reproducible test script.

action= :
  start : begin recording (idempotent — restarts).
  stop  : stop recording.
  dump  : return the recorded sequence in `format`.
          format= playwright | robot | cypress | json
  clear : drop the recording.
  status: returns {recording: bool, count: int}.

  # ... user / agent does pw_act calls ...
  pw_recorder(sid, "dump", format="playwright")
  → returns a runnable .spec.js file as text.

SECRETS: values typed into password fields (or fields whose name / label says
password, token, secret, OTP, PIN, API key…) are NEVER recorded. The script
reads them from the environment instead — process.env.PASSWORD (playwright),

${PASSWORD} taken from %{PASSWORD} — and dump lists them in secret_variables.
pw_page eval calls are kept as COMMENTS, not replayed (arbitrary page scripts
are not user gestures): dump says so in notes; port them by hand if needed.

Use this to turn an exploratory agent run into a CI-ready regression test.

Refused in a SECURE session (pw_session secure=true).

outils.name: pw_observe
outils.title: Pw Observe
outils.description:
Multi-mode page observation with explicit cost/robustness tradeoff.

action= (synonym: mode=) :
  indexed : compact text list — "[0] button "Login"", "[1] input "Email"",
            ... Cheap on tokens. LLM responds with the index. Use as default
            for new pages or when AX cache is empty.
  ax      : same as pw_page(action="inspect", level="lite"). Returns role+name+selector.
            Best when a stable selector matters (caching for AX memory).
  som     : Set-of-Mark — annotated screenshot with numbered boxes overlaid
            on every interactive element. Returns {screenshot, marks: [...]}.
            Use when:
              - the page has canvas/shadow DOM/custom widgets without ARIA
              - AX inspect returned ambiguous results (12x same role+name)
              - previous click attempts failed silently
            Cost: one screenshot pass + numbered overlay rendering.

OUTPUT (indexed mode):
  {
    "mode": "indexed",
    "url": "...",
    "items": [
      {"i": 0, "type": "button", "text": "Login", "selector": "..."},
      {"i": 1, "type": "input",  "text": "Email", "placeholder": "you@x.com", ...},
      ...
    ],
    "step": 7        # use as since_step= for next call to get only diffs
  }

Every item `selector` matches exactly ONE element (checked in the page; made
unique with an :nth-of-type path when the readable one is ambiguous, e.g. four
"edit" links). After the LLM picks an index, dispatch with
pw_act(target=item['target_dsl']) — `target_dsl` is always "css=<selector>".

EXAMPLES:
  pw_observe(sid)                              # indexed, viewport, top 30
  pw_observe(sid, action="som")                # for canvas / ambiguous
  pw_observe(sid, since_step=12)               # only diffs since step 12

In a SECURE session (pw_session secure=true) the css= `target_dsl` is refused: build the target from the item role+name / label / placeholder.

outils.title: Pw Visual
outils.description:
Visual regression: compare the page (or one element) to a "golden" baseline.

First call (or update=true) → records the baseline (baseline_created=true).
Subsequent calls → pixel diff, returning: passed (diff_ratio<=threshold),
diff_ratio, diff_pixels + 3 image URLs (screenshot_url, baseline_url,

you have vision capability. WHERE it changed: diff_regions = up to 10 boxes
{x, y, w, h, pixels} (largest first; diff_regions_total, diff_regions_truncated)
and diff_bbox = one box around all of them, in screenshot pixels of the page
(or of the selector element).

selector=   : narrow to one element (otherwise full page). Synonym: target=.
threshold=  : tolerated ratio of differing pixels (default 0.01 = 1%).
update=true : replace the baseline with the current state (after a deliberate UI change).

outils.name: pw_memory
outils.title: Pw Memory
outils.description:
Query the accumulated AX memory of successfully-used UI paths.

This is how you REUSE what previous runs already learned about a UI
instead of re-discovering it from scratch. Every op returns a COMPACT,
scoped payload — none of them ever dump the whole tree into context.

WHEN TO USE: before navigating a site you may have visited before.
Check action="sites"; if the site is known, ask for a "path" or "find"
what you need rather than blindly inspecting page after page.

OPERATIONS (action=, synonym: op=):
  sites : list known sites + stats (elements, paths, transitions).
          No args. Start here.
  path  : shortest KNOWN click-path to reach a page. Learned from
          every pw_act click / Enter and pw_chain step that changed
          the page (a form submit, a link); direct goto/back/forward
          are not learned (they are not reproducible gestures).
          Required: site=, to_path=.
          Optional: from_path= (default: any OTHER known page — the
                    path always has at least one step),
                    max_depth= (default 6).
          Returns ordered steps {from, to, action_role, action_name,
          action_target, action_selector, verified_count} — feed
          action_target straight into pw_act(target=...).
  find  : search elements by name/role across a site.
          Required: site=, query=. Optional: limit= (default 20).
          Returns compact matches {path, role, name, selector,
          verified_count, stale}.
  page  : known interactive elements of ONE page (not the whole site).
          Required: site=, path=. Optional: limit= (default 50, here
          passed as limit=).
          Returns a flat, capped element list.

site= is the normalized site id from action="sites" (host[:port]).
path= / to_path= / from_path= are URL paths ("/", "/admin/users", …).

EXAMPLES:
  pw_memory(action="sites")
  pw_memory(action="path", site="app.local:8080", to_path="/admin/users")
  pw_memory(action="path", site="app.local:8080", to_path="/billing",
            from_path="/dashboard")
  pw_memory(action="find", site="app.local:8080", query="export")
  pw_memory(action="page", site="app.local:8080", path="/settings")

anyOf.description: Result of pw_memory — query the AX memory store (sites/paths/find/page).

op.description: The memory operation that was dispatched.

outils.name: pw_run
outils.title: Pw Run
outils.description:
Replay a saved PROCEDURE on a browser session without calling you between
gestures: the gestures, fallbacks and checks are executed by a deterministic
interpreter (same code paths as pw_act / pw_login: URL guard, AX memory, secure
session, purging), so a known site task costs ONE call instead of one per click.
A procedure is a behavior tree saved with pw_procedure(action="save").

  pw_run(session_id, procedure="download-statement",
         params={"month": "2026-03", "login": "⟦creds:TOKEN@https://site.example⟧"})

procedure= : id of a procedure of the account (pw_procedure(action="list")).
version=   : a given version; 0 (default) = the latest.
params=    : EVERY parameter the procedure declares, none missing, none extra:
             "string" and "number" values are typed as given; a "creds"
             parameter takes the ⟦creds:TOKEN@ORIGIN⟧ marker the user supplied
             (the origin must be the procedure's) and is only handed to
             pw_login - a password is never a parameter. Wrong or missing
             parameters are refused (params_invalid) BEFORE any gesture.
confirmed= : node paths the user agreed to (see needs_confirmation below).

Each act tries its targets in order and stops at the first that works, then
checks its expect condition. A failing step makes the enclosing sel try its
next alternative; a failure nobody recovers ends the run. A click or key press
whose outcome is uncertain (timeout, service error) is NEVER replayed: the run
stops with failed_at.reason starting "ambiguous". Budget: 60 gesture attempts
and 200 s per run; stopping the call cancels the run between steps.

Returns {ok, status: ok|failed|needs_confirmation|cancelled, procedure, version,
steps: [{path, act, target_used, ok, ms, reason?}], failed_at?: {path, reason,
tried_targets}, node_path?, description?, url, title, duration_ms, attempts}.
- failed: the page is where the run stopped; read failed_at, then continue by
  hand with pw_page / pw_act (and tell the user the procedure needs a fix).
- needs_confirmation: a node marked confirm stopped BEFORE acting. Show
  description to the user; if they agree, call pw_run again with the same
  arguments plus confirmed=[node_path]: the run resumes at that node on the
  same session (the earlier steps are not replayed).
The procedure only acts on its own origin: on any other page its steps fail
(origin_mismatch) - open it first (pw_session / a goto step).

params.description: Every parameter the procedure declares (string, number, or the ⟦creds:TOKEN@ORIGIN⟧ marker for a creds parameter).

confirmed.description: Node paths the user agreed to (from a needs_confirmation result).

anyOf.description: Result of pw_run - a procedure replayed without the LLM.

steps.description: Executed steps {path, act, target_used, ok, ms, reason?}.

failed_at.description: {path, reason, tried_targets} of the failure that ended the run.

node_path.description: needs_confirmation: the node waiting for the user's agreement.

description.description: needs_confirmation: what the node is about to do.

attempts.description: Gesture attempts used of the budget.

anyOf.description:
Typed shape of the error envelope produced by ``_toolkit.err()``.

Mirrors the error contract the chat frontend parses :
  * ``ok`` is the discriminator (False = failure),
  * ``error`` is a stable machine code (snake_case),
  * ``message`` is the human-readable text,
  * ``fix`` is an optional hint how to recover.

Tools declare their return type as ``Union[<SuccessModel>,
ErrEnvelope]`` so FastMCP generates a discriminated union schema
the LLM can pattern-match on the ``ok`` field. The runtime
wire format is unchanged — both branches serialise to the same
JSON dict the frontend already reads.

``extra='allow'`` because ``err()`` lets each call site attach
context (``cmd``, ``path``, ``expected``, ``actual``, …) — these
are kept for the LLM but aren't part of the strict schema.

retryable.description: True iff a retry might succeed (transient error).

outils.name: pw_procedure
outils.title: Pw Procedure
outils.description:
List, read, save or delete the account's PROCEDURES: behavior trees that
pw_run replays on a browser session without calling you between gestures.

  pw_procedure(action="list", origin="https://site.example")  # origin optional
  pw_procedure(action="get", id="download-statement", version=0)   # 0 = latest
  pw_procedure(action="save", procedure={...})   # validated; creates a new version
  pw_procedure(action="delete", id="download-statement", version=0)  # 0 = all versions

FORMAT (JSON):
  {"id": "download-statement",           # slug a-z 0-9 _ -
   "origin": "https://site.example",     # exact http(s) origin, no path
   "version": 1,                         # ignored on save (the next number is used)
   "description": "Download a monthly statement",
   "params": {"month": "string", "login": "creds"},   # string | number | creds
   "root": NODE}
NODE (exactly one key):
  {"seq": [NODE, ...]}      in order, stops at the first failure
  {"sel": [NODE, ...]}      fallback: stops at the first success
  {"if": COND, "then": NODE, "else": NODE}   then/else optional; a lone
                            {"if": COND} (e.g. inside sel) succeeds when COND is true
  {"act": "goto|click|fill|select|press|check|uncheck|hover|wait",
   "t": ["role=link|name=Statements", "text=Statements"],   # targets, tried in order
   "v": "{month}",          # value (fill, select, press key) with {param} templates
   "url": "/statements",    # goto only: a path, or a URL of the SAME origin
   "expect": COND,          # checked after the gesture (default wait 5 s)
   "confirm": true,         # stop for the user's agreement before acting
   "timeout_ms": 8000}
  {"login": {"creds": "{login}", "password_target": "label=Password",
             "username_target": "label=User", "submit_target": "role=button|name=Sign in",
             "wait_for": "role=heading|name=Home"}}   # delegates to pw_login (secure session)
  {"retry": NODE, "max": 3}   {"wait_ms": 500}   (at most 10000)
COND (all given keys must hold): {"url_path": "/statements*", "visible": TARGET,
  "text": "March", "not": COND}   url_path: equality or * wildcard on the path.
RULES: targets are SEMANTIC only (role=, name=, text=, label=, placeholder=,
test_id=, alt=, title=, nth=); css=, xpath= and ref= are refused. {param} may appear
in t, v, url and COND; a "creds" parameter only in login.creds and never a
literal ⟦creds:…⟧ token or password anywhere in the tree. goto/url outside origin are
refused. fill and select need v and t; press needs v; goto needs url; wait needs t.
LIMITS: depth 8, 80 nodes, 30 children per seq/sel, 5 targets per act, strings
300 characters, 12 params, 64 KB, 200 procedures and 50 versions per procedure.
Validation errors list every problem (procedure_invalid): fix and save again.
Returns list {count, procedures: [{id, origin, version, versions, description,
params, updated_at}]}, get {procedure}, save {id, version, nodes}, delete {deleted}.

procedure.description: save: the procedure document (see the format above).

anyOf.description: Result of pw_procedure - list, get, save or delete procedures.

procedures.description: list: latest version of each procedure.
